Resolves #19350

`Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace` composes its default cross-window `window.Participation` for a published `crossWindowSortGroup` — a declinable collaborator in the maximize affordance's shape (`dockParticipation`: `true` lazily imports the engine class; `{module}` composes a host subclass; an instance is adopted; `null` declines) — and owns the lifecycle its seams already drive: composed once the workspace has a window and the sort group, kept across unchanged bindings, re-composed on a window change, a late set, or a host's explicit recompose, destroyed with the workspace. Host seams ride `getDockParticipationConfig()`. The Workstation's main and popup compositions, its participation map and promise, and the per-projection re-creation are deleted; Demo B and the witness harness, which are not façade consumers, are untouched; the Fleet Manager cockpit publishes no sort group and composes nothing. ADR 0029 §2.3 carries the amendment.

Evidence: L1 (the façade's unit spec, the Workstation and Demo B unit tiers) → L2 achieved headless (the Workstation's native pop-out, popup-over-popup and vessel-route e2e witnesses) → L3 required for AC-5 (the Institution's next engine pin). Residual: AC-5, Residual-Owner: neomjs/neo-agent-institution#12 (the FM v1 epic, where the cockpit's pin receipts land).

agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline `pr-body` + `substrate-size` run in CI.

size-guard-growth: src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs — the façade gains the collaborator's declaration (`dockParticipation`), three members, one hook and four lifecycle call sites (+18 code lines, 1220 → 1238); the composition itself lives in the new `window/ParticipationLifecycle.mjs` beside `TearOut.mjs`, and the Workstation loses 129 lines of the same concern.

## Deltas from ticket
- The opt-in is the published `crossWindowSortGroup`, not the tear-out flag: the Workstation's popup workspaces participate with `enableDockTearOutLifecycle` off (they return through their close policy), and gating on the flag turned eight Workstation arms red on the first wide run. The ticket body carries the correction (its author's), the ADR paragraph states it, a positive arm pins it.
- The façade's arms live in their own spec beside the Participation class's (`DockWorkspaceParticipation.spec.mjs`); the ticket named the sibling file.
- `syncDockParticipation({recompose: true})`: a host whose seams changed after construction (the Workstation creates its drag controller and proxy embodiment in `initializeVesselResources`) asks for one re-composition — seam identity is not a binding the façade compares, so the old per-projection re-creation's one real job survives as one explicit call.
- Three e2e barriers waited for the main participation's id to CHANGE after a detach (`e2e/utils/workstationPopOut.mjs` `settleForClaim`, two polls in `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL`); they now assert the inverse — the registered target survives the detach projection — which is the façade's guarantee, and the hazard the barrier guarded (a claim landing on a target the refresh was about to destroy) no longer exists.
- `VesselWorkspace`'s `state.participation` was never assigned in production (only destroyed and nulled); both sites go with the map, and the unit arm that faked it drops that fixture.
- The file-size ratchet refused the façade's first shape (+68 code lines on an over-target file), so the composition moved to `src/dashboard/dock/window/ParticipationLifecycle.mjs` — a function module beside `window/TearOut.mjs`, the sibling precedent (structural pre-flight fast path); the façade keeps the declaration, the members, the hook and two one-line delegates (+18), the baseline carries 1238, and the growth line above says why.

## Test Evidence
Headless e2e, outside CI (the Workstation witnesses are selected only with `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`): `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL` (3 arms), `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL` and `VesselNativeRouteNL`: 6 of 6 green at the head with the flipped barriers (red before the flip on exactly the three arms that polled for a re-creation); `WorkstationPopOutPaneIdentityNL` and `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL` green; `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` 2 passed / 2 failed — the two large-over-small arms are red on dev (#19297, Ada's stale proxy assertion), the same two before this branch.

## Evolution
The gate pivoted once, on evidence: the ticket (and the record author's framing) placed the composition under the tear-out lifecycle; the first wide unit run showed the popup workspaces participating without it, and the engine class already named the sort group as the registry identity — so the sort group is the opt-in and the flag plays no part.
